name: Oracle Database
description: Oracle Database 12c and later (11g through overlays), including Autonomous Database and Oracle 23ai Free. One connection is one database (or pluggable database), so the hierarchy has one level, schema. Reads the ALL_ dictionary views, which every user can query and which show exactly what that user may see.

version.sql: select version_full as version, product || ' ' || version_full as banner from product_component_version where product like 'Oracle%'

alternatives.sql: select version as version, product || ' ' || version as banner from product_component_version where product like 'Oracle%'

test.sql: select user as login, sys_context('USERENV', 'CON_NAME') as container, sys_context('USERENV', 'DB_NAME') as db_name from dual

source.sql: select 'Oracle Database' as product, version_full as version, product || ' ' || version_full as banner, user as login from product_component_version where product like 'Oracle%'

sql: select u.username as name, to_char(u.created, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') as created_at
tc.comments as "comment", o.owner as owner, t.num_rows as row_count,
left join all_tables t on t.owner = o.owner and t.table_name = o.object_name and o.object_type = 'TABLE'
left join all_views v on v.owner = o.owner and v.view_name = o.object_name and o.object_type = 'VIEW'
left join all_tab_comments tc on tc.owner = o.owner and tc.table_name = o.object_name
where o.owner = {{schema}} and o.object_type in ('TABLE', 'VIEW', 'MATERIALIZED VIEW')
and o.secondary = 'N' and o.object_name not like 'BIN$%'
and not (o.object_type = 'TABLE' and exists (select 1 from all_mviews m
where m.owner = o.owner and m.mview_name = o.object_name))
select c.table_name as dataset, c.column_id as ordinal, c.column_name as name,
when c.data_type = 'NUMBER' and c.data_precision is not null
then '(' || c.data_precision || ',' || nvl(c.data_scale, 0) || ')' end as data_type,
c.nullable as nullable, c.data_default as default_value, cc.comments as "comment",
case when c.identity_column = 'YES' or c.virtual_column = 'YES' then 'Y' else 'N' end as is_generated,
c.char_length as max_length, c.data_precision as numeric_precision, c.data_scale as numeric_scale
on cc.owner = c.owner and cc.table_name = c.table_name and cc.column_name = c.column_name
where c.owner = {{schema}} and c.table_name in ({{datasets}}) and c.hidden_column = 'NO'
select c.table_name as dataset, c.constraint_name as name,
case c.constraint_type when 'P' then 'primary_key' when 'U' then 'unique'
when 'R' then 'foreign_key' else 'check' end as type,
cc.column_name as columns, r.owner as ref_schema, r.table_name as ref_dataset,
rc.column_name as ref_columns, nvl(cc.position, 0) as seq, c.search_condition_vc as definition
on cc.owner = c.owner and cc.constraint_name = c.constraint_name and cc.table_name = c.table_name
left join all_constraints r on r.owner = c.r_owner and r.constraint_name = c.r_constraint_name
on rc.owner = r.owner and rc.constraint_name = r.constraint_name and rc.position = cc.position
where c.owner = {{schema}} and c.table_name in ({{datasets}}) and c.constraint_type in ('P', 'U', 'R', 'C')
and not (c.constraint_type = 'C' and c.search_condition_vc like '% IS NOT NULL')
select i.table_name as dataset, i.index_name as name,
case when i.uniqueness = 'UNIQUE' then 'Y' else 'N' end as is_unique,
case when exists (select 1 from all_constraints k where k.owner = i.table_owner
and k.index_name = i.index_name and k.constraint_type = 'P') then 'Y' else 'N' end as is_primary,
lower(i.index_type) as method, ic.column_name as columns, ic.column_position as seq
join all_ind_columns ic on ic.index_owner = i.owner and ic.index_name = i.index_name
select o.object_name as name, lower(o.object_type) as type, 'PL/SQL' as language, o.owner as owner
select d.name as dataset, d.referenced_owner as upstream_schema, d.referenced_name as upstream_dataset,
where d.owner = {{schema}} and d.type in ('VIEW', 'MATERIALIZED VIEW')
select u.username as name, 'user' as type,
case when u.account_status = 'OPEN' then 'Y' else 'N' end as can_login

alternatives.sql: select u.username as name, 'user' as type from all_users u where u.oracle_maintained = 'N' order by u.username

sql: select p.table_name as dataset, p.grantee as principal, p.privilege as privilege,
lower(p.type) as object_type, p.grantor as grantor, p.grantable as grantable
select p.object_name as dataset, p.policy_name as name, 'row_access' as type,
p.pf_owner || '.' || nvl2(p.package, p.package || '.', '') || p.function as definition,
select s.table_name as dataset, s.column_name as field,
case when t.num_rows > 0 then s.num_nulls / t.num_rows end as null_fraction,
s.num_distinct as distinct_count, s.avg_col_len as avg_width
join all_tables t on t.owner = s.owner and t.table_name = s.table_name

sample.sql: select * from {{schema|ident}}.{{dataset|ident}} fetch first {{limit|int}} rows only

overlays.description: Oracle 11g: no FETCH FIRST, no oracle_maintained, no identity columns, no search_condition_vc, no text_vc.

schemas.sql: select u.username as name from all_users u order by u.username

sql: tc.comments as "comment", o.owner as owner, t.num_rows as row_count
left join all_tables t on t.owner = o.owner and t.table_name = o.object_name and o.object_type = 'TABLE'
left join all_tab_comments tc on tc.owner = o.owner and tc.table_name = o.object_name
where o.owner = {{schema}} and o.object_type in ('TABLE', 'VIEW', 'MATERIALIZED VIEW')
and o.secondary = 'N' and o.object_name not like 'BIN$%'
select c.table_name as dataset, c.column_id as ordinal, c.column_name as name, c.data_type as data_type,
c.nullable as nullable, cc.comments as "comment", c.char_length as max_length,
c.data_precision as numeric_precision, c.data_scale as numeric_scale
on cc.owner = c.owner and cc.table_name = c.table_name and cc.column_name = c.column_name
select c.table_name as dataset, c.constraint_name as name,
case c.constraint_type when 'P' then 'primary_key' when 'U' then 'unique' else 'foreign_key' end as type,
cc.column_name as columns, r.owner as ref_schema, r.table_name as ref_dataset,
rc.column_name as ref_columns, cc.position as seq
on cc.owner = c.owner and cc.constraint_name = c.constraint_name and cc.table_name = c.table_name
left join all_constraints r on r.owner = c.r_owner and r.constraint_name = c.r_constraint_name
on rc.owner = r.owner and rc.constraint_name = r.constraint_name and rc.position = cc.position
where c.owner = {{schema}} and c.table_name in ({{datasets}}) and c.constraint_type in ('P', 'U', 'R')

principals.sql: select u.username as name, 'user' as type from all_users u order by u.username
